title: Volts to Watts Calculator (with Amps) | Wattlyst
meta: Turn volts and amps into watts for DC or AC circuits. Includes power factor for AC loads and worked examples for 12V, 24V and 230V.
author: ali-ahmad

p: Watts are volts times amps, adjusted by the power factor on AC. 230 V × 5 A = 1,150 VA; a heater turns all of it into 1,150 W, a motor at a power factor of 0.8 only 920 W of useful power.
Rearranged, the same formula gives amps = watts ÷ volts and volts = watts ÷ amps. The watts to amps calculator and the amps to watts calculator do those directions.

Volts alone have no watts. Voltage is the electrical pressure; watts appear only when current flows. A 230 V socket with nothing plugged in delivers zero watts; with 5 A of heating load it delivers 1,150 W. The same applies to an older 220 V figure: 10 A there is 2,200 W at a power factor of one.

sections.h2: 12 volts to watts and other DC systems
p: For batteries, solar panels and car circuits choose DC. 12 V × 5 A = 60 W, and 24 V × 10 A = 240 W. A higher battery voltage carries the same power with fewer amps, which is why larger inverters run on higher-voltage banks.

sections.h2: Watts, volts, amps triangle and Ohm's law
p: The power triangle (P = V × I) links watts, volts and amps: cover the one you want and the other two show how to get it. Ohm's law (V = I × R) links volts, amps and resistance. Together they answer most circuit questions: for a pure resistance such as a heater element, watts also equal amps squared × ohms, and volts squared ÷ ohms.

Ohm's law applies directly only to resistive loads. Motors, chargers and LED drivers do not behave like a fixed resistance, so for them measure or read the current and use watts = volts × amps × power factor.

faq.q: How do I convert volts to watts?
faq.a: Multiply volts by amps, then by the power factor on AC. 230 V × 5 A × 0.8 = 920 W. Without the current there is no answer.
None on its own. Watts depend on the current: 5 A at 230 V is 1,150 W for a heater and 920 W for a motor at a power factor of 0.8.
It depends on the amps. At 5 A, 12 V gives 60 W; double the current and the watts double.

faq.q: How do I convert volts to amps?
faq.a: Divide the watts by the volts (and the power factor on AC): amps = watts ÷ (volts × power factor). The watts to amps calculator does this for DC, single-phase and three-phase.

faq.q: What is the watts, volts, amps triangle?
faq.a: Watts = volts × amps, volts = watts ÷ amps, amps = watts ÷ volts. On AC multiply the volts × amps side by the power factor.

faq.q: Is this an Ohm's law calculator?
faq.a: It covers the power side of Ohm's law: watts from volts and amps. Ohm's law itself, V = I × R, links volts, amps and resistance and holds exactly only for resistive loads such as heater elements.

key_facts: Watts = volts × amps × power factor. 230 V × 5 A at a power factor of 0.8 is 920 W.
On DC there is no power factor: 12 V × 5 A = 60 W and 24 V × 10 A = 240 W.
At the same 5 A, a 230 V heater gives 1,150 W, while a 12 V battery load gives a small fraction of that: higher voltage moves more power through the same current.
Voltage on its own is not power. A 230 V socket supplies only as many watts as the connected load draws in amps.
mistakes: Asking how many watts a voltage is. Voltage alone has no power; you need the current the load draws.
Multiplying volts × amps for a motor and calling it watts. That is VA; the real watts are lower by the power factor (about 0.8).
Using Ohm's law with a fixed resistance for a motor, charger or LED driver. Their resistance is not constant; use the measured current instead.
Forgetting √3 on three-phase. The 400 V row in the table already includes it.

examples.title: 12 volts to watts at 5 A (DC)
examples.text: 12 V × 5 A = 60 W, about what a small DC fan or a router with a few lights draws.

examples.title: 24 V system at 10 A
examples.text: 24 V × 10 A = 240 W from a 24 V battery bank.

examples.title: 230 V and 5 A, heating load
examples.text: 230 V × 5 A × 1 = 1,150 W, roughly an electric iron or small room heater.

examples.title: 230 V and 5 A, motor or mixed load
examples.text: 230 V × 5 A = 1,150 VA; × 0.8 = 920 W of real power. The cable still carries the full 5 A.

examples.title: How many watts is 220 volts at 10 A?
examples.text: 220 V × 10 A × 1 = 2,200 W for a resistive load.

content.answer: 230 volts at 5 amps is 1,150 VA, which is 920 watts at a power factor of 0.8 or 1,150 W for a heater. Watts = volts × amps × power factor. Volts alone do not give watts: you need the current too. On DC the power factor is one, so 12 V at 5 A is 60 W.

formula.text: P = V × I (DC);  P = V × I × PF (single-phase AC);  P = √3 × V × I × PF (three-phase AC);  Ohm's law: V = I × R
lines: PF = power factor (1 for DC and heaters)
R = resistance in ohms (Ω); V × I without PF is the apparent power in VA

content.safety: Measuring live voltage and current at the mains is dangerous. Use a clamp meter rated for the circuit, keep to battery and plug-in measurements yourself, and let a licensed electrician take readings inside a distribution board.
